newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-De La Rue results top of expectations.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-De La Rue results top of expectations.

text.p: British printing and security products group De La Rue Plc on Tuesday announced first-half results at the top end of analysts' expectations, noting that it saw signs of further stabilisation in banknote prices.

The company posted pretax profits of 60.3 million pounds ($100 million) for the half -- sharply lower than last year's 69.1 million, but higher than estimates, which ranged from 55 to 61 million pounds.
De La Rue also raised its dividend to 7.5 pence per share from 7.25 in the year-ago period.
"There are no surprises. Although there's a reduction in profits, we are at the top end of forecasts," chief executive Jeremy Marshall told Reuters in an interview.
The company's shares rose on the news, gaining 2.5 pence to 557.5 pence by 1135 GMT after touching an intraday high of 579 pence earlier.
On Monday, the stock scraped 542 pence, its lowest level since September 1992 as investors nervously awaited the results, which the company had warned would be down from last year.
Marshall said banknote prices appeared to have stabilised further since June.
At that time, the firm cautioned that difficult trading conditions in its cash systems division and low banknote prices would hit its first-half results.
"We do have clear signs that the average prices we are obtaining are stabilising," Marshall said.
"Up until June, we did see some deterioration in margins because prices were going up, mainly because we're putting additional security features into notes," he added.
Banknote volumes increased by 14.5 percent in the first half ended September 30, compared to the year-ago period.
"We are meeting competition on the banknote side. But the group (De La Rue) on the whole is making margins of 12 percent," Marshall said.
In its cash systems division, the company said it was beginning to see considerable benefits from reorganisations and new products coming to market.
"The fact that we've put up the dividend is an indication that we're confident in the fundamentals of the business," Marshall said. He declined to make full-year forecasts.
Analysts currently expected the firm to post pretax profits of about 139 million pounds for the year, down six percent from last year, according to Edinburgh Financial Publishing. ($1=.5970 Pound)
